name: Genre-specific micro preset and MIDI packs for acid, EBM and dark disco
pain: Producers want small, focused packs for one sound, such as acid patches with matching MIDI patterns, EBM bass racks, or aggrotech and rave-EBM drums. Existing packs are broad, or tutorials stop short of giving usable sounds.
who_pays: Bedroom and semi-pro techno, acid and EBM producers using Serum, Vital or Ableton racks
pay_signal: Explicit 'I'd buy that' for a Serum acid micro pack with MIDI patterns (577). EBM racks are already sold through a shop with discount codes (599). Repeated requests for niche drum sounds and sample sources (608, 609, 591).
product_idea: Build it: 'Inch of Shadow' micro packs, each with about 30 Vital/Serum patches plus a MIDI groove library plus Ableton racks, for acid lines, EBM sequenced bass and dark disco drums. Use it: his own studio patches become the source material. Note the Vital version mismatch problem (586) and ship patches for the stable version.
known_competitors: Studio Brootle EBM racks (599); tutorial-channel packs (577, 586)
check_next: List acid/EBM micro packs on Gumroad and Splice and their prices. Post a free 5-patch EBM bass teaser and measure email signups.

crowding.reason: Acid Serum preset+MIDI packs and EBM Serum/Ableton rack packs already exist from several sellers at about $10-$40, plus free EBM racks and free Vital acid presets; only dark disco and aggrotech preset+MIDI packs look thin, and their demand is unproven.

name: All-in-one analysis meter M4L device (scope, stereo, spectrum, key)
pain: Ableton lacks a native oscilloscope. Many viewers ask which stereo, phase or spectrum meter a creator uses. Users want key finding inside the meter they already bought, but the existing key finder M4L device has a poor interface.
who_pays: Ableton Suite users doing sound design, mixing and their own mastering
pay_signal: One user bought Swiss Army Meter days ago and still wants a key finder and a slim mode (642). Another says 'gonna buy it' (644). Repeated 'what is that meter' questions (628, 631, 637, 652, 622).
product_idea: Both. Use it: Swiss Army Meter for now. Build it: a compact M4L 'scope + correlation + key/scale finder' strip with a slim mode, aimed at synth patching and mixdown checks.
known_competitors: Swiss Army Meter (Noir Labs), JB KeyFinder (642)
check_next: Test Swiss Army Meter for missing features. Prototype key detection in Max using an existing pitch-class approach and check its accuracy on his own stems.

crowding.reason: Scope, stereo and spectrum meters are crowded and cheap (Swiss Army Meter at $10, Decibel, SPAN) and key finding is covered (free Live Key, JB KeyFinder at $4+); only the scope + key + slim-mode combo looks unserved, and whether Swiss Army Meter or native Live 12 already cover it is unchecked.

A reviewer called Swiss Army Meter an absolute steal at $3 versus about $200 for iZotope Insight

name: Live-performance helper devices for Ableton (momentary FX, reverb kill, chain overview, macro curves)
pain: Live players find momentary effects fiddly to set up through drum racks and MIDI mapping. They cannot instantly kill reverb tails, cannot view a whole FX chain at once mid-set, cannot launch clips immediately yet quantized, and want more than 16 macros with custom mapping curves.
who_pays: Ableton users performing live hybrid sets with controllers or Push
pay_signal: Users explicitly ask for an M4L or third-party fix (4). One user would pay to stop using Stream Deck (668). Users have paid for Suite but build clunky workarounds (20, 31).
product_idea: Build it: a 'Perform Kit' M4L bundle with these parts: a one-knob momentary FX throw, a reverb/delay tail kill, a remote chain-parameter overview, and a macro mapper with curves and banks. He can use it in his own live sets.
known_competitors: ClyphX Pro, Isotonik devices, Cycling74 audio routing devices (12)
check_next: Search maxforlive.com for momentary-FX and macro-curve devices and read their reviews. Prototype the reverb kill first, since it is the smallest scope.

crowding.reason: Macro curves/banks are covered by Ableton's Performer (included with Live 12 Suite) plus free maxforlive.com mappers, and momentary FX already has paid and free devices; only tail-kill/chain-overview remain unchecked.

competitors.name: Ableton Performance Pack (Performer, Variations) by Iftah

name: Voice / natural-language control of Ableton
pain: Producers want to control Ableton by talking to it, for example for technical how-to questions or hands-free operation. The need is strongest for users with visual impairment or a missing hand. The demo device people saw is not released.
who_pays: Ableton users with accessibility needs, beginners, and Stream Deck users
pay_signal: 'Is this something you are selling', 'I'd love to try' (675). 'I'd be very interested in getting one' (671). Repeated 'please release' and 'when' comments (659, 673).
product_idea: Build it: an M4L device plus a local bridge that maps spoken commands to Live API actions (create track, load device, arm, set tempo, answer how-to questions). Build it with Claude Code.
known_competitors: Unreleased demo device in video (659); Stream Deck plugins (51, 668)
check_next: Check whether the demo creator released anything. Check Ableton's terms for LLM-driven control. Estimate token cost per command (674).

crowding.reason: The planned Max for Live + AI bridge already exists free (Producer Pal, two ableton-mcp projects) and VIXSOUND and Grip already sell voice control; no proof found that anyone pays for voice control itself.

name: Loop prep tool for hardware samplers (BPM-stretch, slice, export for Tonverk/Digitakt)
pain: The Tonverk has no time-stretch or BPM detection. Users want time-stretch and slicing without workarounds, the Digitakt II caps slices at 64, Bitwig's sampler has no time-stretch, and getting samples onto boxes is clunky.
who_pays: Elektron and other groovebox owners who use loops and breaks
pay_signal: Users bought $1,300+ hardware and still need external workarounds (107, 74). Someone built a free iOS uploader because no tool existed (116).
product_idea: Build it: a web tool that takes a loop, detects BPM, time-stretches it to a target tempo, auto-slices it to a grid that fits the box's limits, and exports a pre-sliced WAV or slice chain. Use it for his own hardware jams.
known_competitors: Ableton warp and resample; Elektron Transfer; Model-TG uploader (116)
check_next: Confirm the Tonverk and Digitakt II slice and file formats. Test the quality of browser time-stretching (Rubber Band compiled to WebAssembly).

crowding.reason: DigiChain is one dominant free option that already chains, slices to grid limits (including Tonverk) and time-stretches; ReCycle and Elektron Transfer are also free, and no one is shown paying for a hardware loop-prep tool.

name: Elektron project, song mode and sample management companion
pain: Digitakt II users cannot keep a computer folder in sync with the box's samples. They had to re-enter Song Mode manually when merging songs into one live project. They cannot change a sound once and have it apply across patterns. Old firmware versions are not archived.
who_pays: Digitakt II, Digitone II and Tonverk owners writing full tracks or live sets
pay_signal: One user asks outright for a 'Song Mode mgmt tool' and already uses elk-herd (124). Owners of expensive hardware repeatedly complain about the workflow (120, 121, 552).
product_idea: Build it: a desktop or web companion that exports and imports Song Mode as text, does a sample diff and sync against a folder, and reports per-pattern parameter changes. Feasibility depends on Elektron's SysEx for MK2 devices. Use it: elk-herd for DT1.
check_next: Research whether the Digitakt II SysEx project format has been reverse-engineered (check the elk-herd repo and firmware mod scene, 111, 486).

crowding.reason: Free tools (elk-herd, Elektron Transfer, ALISEO, Elektroid) already cover sample and project management; Song Mode is unserved but seems blocked because song data can't be read from the device, and the only paid tool found ($8.99 SaveProj) has 0 ratings.

name: MIDI clock sync diagnostics and fixer
pain: Synths and grooveboxes drift or fail to lock to external clock. Arpeggiators start off-clock, sequencers do not start or reset, and some setups have duplicate-note bugs. Users cannot tell which device is at fault.
who_pays: DAWless and hybrid hardware producers recording jams to Ableton
pay_signal: One user is considering buying a Multiclock and MRCC because jitter is a dealbreaker (95). A paid-app review asks for MIDI clock input (281). Owners of paid gear push vendors for fixes (69).
product_idea: Build it: a Web MIDI clock analyzer that measures jitter and drift, logs start, stop and SPP messages, and finds the device at fault. An optional M4L clock sender could start transport with an offset. Use it: Multiclock if a hardware master clock is needed.
known_competitors: E-RM Multiclock, MRCC (95), generic MIDI monitors
check_next: Check whether a clock-jitter tester for Web MIDI already exists. Measure Chrome's Web MIDI timestamp precision on macOS.

crowding.reason: Hardware fixers are crowded (Multiclock, midiclock+, Midronome, MRCC) and clearly paid for, but fault-finding diagnostics have only weak or free tools and no sourced proof that anyone pays for diagnostics alone

competitors.name: MidiBus (iOS clock generator + clock accuracy monitor)

name: Live set transitions and per-song tempo/scene management
pain: Loading the next Live set stops the music. Bitwig can only have one song active. Bitwig 6 lost per-scene tempo. Hardware sequencers cannot switch projects on the downbeat. Moving from session to arrangement is a chore.
who_pays: Live electronic performers using Ableton, Bitwig or hardware sequencers
pay_signal: Performers with paid rigs (Push, UAD, Eloquencer) build elaborate workarounds such as a second drum machine or reset clocks (32, 165, 176).
product_idea: Build it: an M4L 'setlist' device that turns one large set into navigable songs, with per-song tempo, key notes and a scene-range jump, plus a session-to-arrangement recorder helper. Use it for his own live shows.
known_competitors: ClyphX Pro, Setlist-type M4L devices (not in posts)
check_next: Interview 3 to 5 live performers about their song-change workflow. Review existing setlist M4L devices on maxforlive.com.

crowding.reason: Ableton per-song navigation and tempo already covered by native scene tempo, AbleSet ($129-$269), ClyphX Pro (£66), Scene Setlist and several free M4L setlist devices; Bitwig and hardware gaps were not checked and the M4L idea does not serve them.

who_pays: Ableton producers who write sequences and chord-based tracks

name: Stem and multitrack export and QC
pain: Engineers spend too long checking stems for sync, missing audio, odd stereo, mismatched lengths and bad naming. Beginners do not know how to group stems. Groovebox users cannot get per-track stems with master FX, and sampler apps cannot export performed stems.
who_pays: Self-mixing producers, assistant engineers, and groovebox users sending stems to mixers
pay_signal: A paid-app user demands stem export (259). An assistant engineer describes a recurring time cost (194). Elektron owners search for workarounds (125, 140).
product_idea: Build it: a drag-and-drop web tool that checks a stem folder for sample rate, length and offset alignment, silence, mono-in-stereo and naming. It outputs a report and a renaming template. Use it for his own exports to collaborators and mastering.
known_competitors: None named in posts; DAW batch export
check_next: Ask r/audioengineering what QC tools engineers use. Prototype the checker with the Web Audio API on his own stem folders.

crowding.reason: Stem Checker already does exactly this (length, silence, dual-mono, sample rate, batch rename), has been reviewed by Sound On Sound, and offers a free drag-and-drop browser version, with AudioQC, MonoChecker and MonoMate overlapping.
